possible_risks.description: Lack of model transparency is due to insufficient documentation of the model design, development, and evaluation process and the absence of insights into the inner workings of the model.
possible_risks.justification: Card provides only architecture, modality, access, and license; no training data, evaluation, or development details are stated for this checkpoint.

possible_risks.description: AI model risks are socio-technical, so their testing needs input from a broad set of disciplines and diverse testing practices.
possible_risks.justification: No reported evaluations or testing practices are documented for this checkpoint, so testing diversity cannot be established.

possible_risks.description: Testing is unrepresentative when the test inputs are mismatched with the inputs that are expected during deployment.
possible_risks.justification: No deployment context or evaluation data is described, so any risk testing would be unrepresentative relative to unspecified intended use.

possible_risks.description: Since foundation models can be used for many purposes, a model's intended use is important for defining the relevant risks of that model. As the use changes, the relevant risks might correspondingly change.
possible_risks.justification: The card does not state intended use or downstream tasks, leaving the relevant risk profile undefined.

possible_risks.description: Proper documentation contains information about how a model's data was collected, curated, and used to train a model, including any synthetic data generation processes. Without proper documentation it might be harder to satisfactorily explain the behavior of the model.
possible_risks.justification: The card does not describe training data collection, curation, or synthetic generation for this checkpoint.
